request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 25-year-old female
Admission date: [DATE]
Discharge date: [DATE]
Length of stay: [NUMBER] days
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of acute onset of epigastric pain and nausea with bilious emesis. Initial workup did not demonstrate evidence of biliary or gallbladder pathology. However, her symptoms progressed and she was re-evaluated with a computed tomography that demonstrated a soft tissue mass located posterior to the gallbladder. Further evaluation with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography observed a complex cystic structure of indeterminate etiology at the porta hepatis.

The patient underwent surgery, during which a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass attached to the infundibulum of the gallbladder was identified and resected. A cholecystectomy was also performed due to inflammation from the hemorrhagic mass. Gross pathology and histology revealed a hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue, and localized cholecystitis in the area adjacent to the mass was also observed.

The patient's postoperative course was uneventful and her symptoms resolved immediately. She was discharged home on the first postoperative day and was asymptomatic when seen in follow-up.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to remove the hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue and cholecystitis. She was discharged with instructions to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient was asymptomatic and in stable condition at the time of discharge.

Discharge Medications: N/A

Follow-up:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission was a hemorrhagic ectopic liver tissue mass attached to the gallbladder infundibulum. It caused the epigastric pain and vomiting and led to the surgery. Localized cholecystitis was an associated finding, but the mass was the primary pathology.

Ectopic liver tissue is a congenital malformation. In ICD-10-AM, "Accessory liver" or ectopic liver tissue falls under Q44.7, "Other congenital malformations of liver", within the Q44 category (congenital malformations of gallbladder, bile ducts and liver). The ICD-10 index lists "Ectopic... liver" under Q44.7, though I'm less certain of the index entry than of the category.

The alternative is K82 (other diseases of gallbladder) or K81 (cholecystitis). However, the histology identified benign ectopic liver tissue as the cause of the inflammation, and the cholecystitis was localized and secondary to the mass. The congenital malformation is therefore the principal diagnosis.

CODE: Q44
